chapter: CBS, return to Ellington and retirement
title: Refusing to take up the horn again
summary: He would not play Dixieland, has only a mouthpiece, and says he no longer has the desire.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Well, in that particular instance, that doesn't mean that you have to participate in that kind
of a situation in order to play your horn, does it?

Well, the -- if you don't participate in that, why it's -- the other kind would be too strenuous for an old man to keep up that. That's why I said we could get -- Barney and I could get a little Dixieland group or something and go someplaces and play Dixieland, and once in a while throw in a sweet tune, or a tune we know or people know, and succeed maybe. But I just don't feel like trying anymore.
But you said that you don't want to play Dixieland.

No, I never could play Dixieland. In fact, when I started out, it was a rebelling against Dixieland, that I started playing as I did. So, but now I just don't care to -- just don't care to play anything.
No. No. I think I got a mouthpiece around somewhere, but outside of that B- I think I brought a mouthpiece with me -- but outside of that I don't have any interest in it at all.

Oh, that's too bad. I hope you'll change your position back to where it was a few weeks ago. Your -- your opinion on music, or your position seems to change from time to time. I can remember one time I ran into you I think when you were working in Washington. You were in Los Angeles briefly, and I ran into you on the street.

And I asked you if you were playing and you said that you weren't. And I said I wished you were. And you said, no, no, no. I'm not a musician. I'm a businessman. And yet you sometimes leave your businessman stance and go back to playing beautiful music. It could happen again, couldn't it?

I like beautiful music, but no, not for me to participate in, I don't think. No, I don't think I could ever develop enough interest in it. You have to want to do something in order to be able to do something, and unless you have a terrific desire for it, I just couldn't perform in the way that I know it should be performed.
